quiz.title: Unit 7 SAQ 02
quiz.headline: World War I and the colonies
quiz.prompt: Answer all parts of the question.
quiz.instructions: Answer all three parts. For each part, Answer the question directly, Prove it with specific historical evidence, and Explain how the evidence supports your answer. On the AP exam each part earns one point. This is self-assessment practice, not official College Board scoring.
quiz.note: Original Page One practice in AP short-answer format. Model answers show one strong response; other accurate, well-supported answers can earn the point.

scaffold.label: Answer
scaffold.text: Respond directly to the task verb: identify, describe, or explain.

scaffold.label: Prove
scaffold.text: Name a specific person, place, institution, or development.

scaffold.label: Explain
scaffold.text: Show how or why the evidence answers the question.

parts.prompt: Identify ONE way governments mobilized their societies for total war during World War I.
criteria: States a specific policy or practice.

model.answer: Governments used conscription to build mass armies.
model.prove: Britain introduced conscription in 1916, and France, Germany, and Russia drafted millions of men.
model.explain: Drafting such large numbers shifted the war from the small professional armies of earlier conflicts to the mobilization of whole societies.

parts.alternatives: Answers can also identify rationing, state control of industry, propaganda, or the recruitment of women to work in factories.

parts.prompt: Describe ONE role that colonial subjects played in World War I.
criteria: Names a specific group or region.

model.answer: Soldiers from the British Empire fought on several fronts.
model.prove: About 1.3 million Indian soldiers served in Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, and soldiers from Senegal and other French colonies fought in France.
model.explain: Their service supplied manpower to the Allies and also gave colonial peoples expectations about their rights after the war.

parts.alternatives: Answers can also describe Chinese laborers who worked behind the lines in France or African porters who carried supplies in East Africa.

parts.prompt: Explain ONE way the outcome of World War I contributed to anticolonial movements after 1919.
criteria: Names a specific event, place, or movement.
Explains how the war's outcome or peace settlement encouraged it.

model.answer: The peace settlement raised hopes of self-determination that it did not meet in the colonies.
model.prove: When the Paris Peace Conference gave Germany's rights in Shandong to Japan, Chinese students protested in the May Fourth Movement of 1919, and in India the Amritsar massacre of 1919 deepened opposition to British rule.
model.explain: Wilson's call for self-determination applied mainly to Europe, so colonial leaders concluded that they would have to press for independence themselves.

parts.alternatives: Answers can also explain Arab disappointment with the mandates in the Middle East or the growth of nationalist parties among colonial veterans.
